title: Community Explorer: Maps, Evidence & Place — Parent Plan

baseline.interpretation: The completed History–Social Science Baseline remains Rory’s starting record. This seven-week course provides Grade 3 instruction and gathers new work evidence through maps, timelines, source analysis, civic problem solving, and a culminating community case.
strengths: Sampled knowledge of basic economics, including goods, services, resources, and trade
Useful prior ideas about communities and evidence that can be extended in Grade 3 work
reinforceThroughUse: Map scale and locating California and the Pacific Ocean
Chronological sequencing and placing an event between dated events
Comparing sources or accounts that disagree
Matching shared public needs to local government services
newGrade3Instruction: The role of legislatures and constructive civic participation
Distinct Indigenous peoples, continuing communities, and careful source attribution
Local geography and history inquiry using maps, photographs, records, and other sources
Applying economics to geography, resources, and community interdependence
baseline.preservation: Course code never writes to roryBaseline2026_history. Do not convert the baseline into a course grade or recreate missing answers.

weeks.parentRole: Prepare simple map markers and an optional U.S. outline map. Ask Rory to point to the key or scale when he explains an answer.
lookFor: Uses a key and cardinal directions
Treats one map space as two blocks consistently
Locates California west of Massachusetts and names the Pacific Ocean
exitIntent: Evidence language tied to a map feature

weeks.parentRole: Prepare dated cards and let Rory move them. Read the fictional source cards aloud without telling him which claim to choose.
lookFor: Uses dates instead of guessing order
Separates a source fact from an inference
Checks a disputed memory against relevant dated evidence
exitIntent: A claim that names its supporting source

weeks.parentRole: Offer fictional or public examples so Rory never has to disclose private family or migration history.
lookFor: Explains that a tradition is meaningful and passed on
Distinguishes migration from short travel
Names culture that can move without being packed

weeks.parentRole: Guide the mock vote and explain that actual lawmaking has more steps. Use the official government links for adult background.
lookFor: Matches a public need to a relevant service
Uses measured data in a civic proposal
States that a legislature discusses and votes on proposed laws

weeks.parentRole: Lead the source lab. Use a tribe-authored or other reliable official source; verify spelling, attribution, present-day language, and the exact claim Rory records.
lookFor: Understands that Indigenous peoples are distinct and present today
Does not infer a specific cultural practice from geography alone
Names the source for every specific community claim
exitIntent: Evidence of continuity into the present
No invented ceremony, belief, quotation, vocabulary, or homeland boundary

weeks.parentRole: Set up resource and trade cards. Ask what the fictional maps actually show before Rory proposes a job or adaptation.
lookFor: Builds a resource → job → good/service chain
Explains how trade can benefit both communities
Uses may/could when a map supports a possibility rather than a fact

weeks.parentRole: Provide two verified dated sources and listen to Rory’s three-to-five-minute case presentation. Prompt only as needed and record the actual help used.
lookFor: Uses map, timeline, and source clues together
Separates observation from inference
Explains one idea that changed after checking evidence
Cites any specific Indigenous community fact
exitIntent: Culminating evidence rather than a placement score
One skill to observe again during regular Grade 3 instruction
